reference: An algorithm is an ordered set of instructions for carrying out a task. Our sorting algorithm asks one clear question at a time. Each answer chooses the next branch. A useful question has a reliable yes-or-no answer based on an observable property, such as the number of sides.

reference: Before asking whether a shape is square, restrict our collection to four-sided polygons. Curved outlines and triangles need other branches. reference: A counterexample is one valid case that shows a proposed always-rule is false. A non-square rectangle disproves the claim that four right angles alone identify a square. One counterexample is enough to reject that claim, even if many squares happened to pass the test correctly.
